name: Subword Tokenization Evaluation (UniMorph Labeller)
description: The popular subword tokenizers of current language models, such as Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), are known not to respect morpheme boundaries, which affects the downstream performance of the models. While many improved tokenization algorithms have been proposed, their evaluation and cross-comparison is still an open problem. As a solution, we propose a combined intrinsic-extrinsic evaluation framework for subword tokenization. Intrinsic evaluation is based on our new UniMorph Labeller tool that classifies subword tokenization as either morphological or alien. Extrinsic evaluation, in turn, is performed via the Out-of-Vocabulary Generalization Challenge 1.0 benchmark, which consists of three newly specified downstream text classification tasks. Our empirical findings show that the accuracy of UniMorph Labeller is 98%, and that, in all language models studied (including ALBERT, BERT, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa), alien tokenization leads to poorer generalizations compared to morphological tokenization for semantic compositionality of word meanings.
evaluation_method: accuracy (intrinsic classification) and accuracy on downstream text-classification tasks
typical_sota_score: 98% (UniMorph Labeller intrinsic accuracy); downstream task SOTA varies / not established
reputation: A recent research benchmark introduced on arXiv with limited adoption so far; cited within tokenization/morphology work but not a community standard.
notes: Intrinsic evaluation depends on UniMorph resources (language coverage limited); extrinsic evaluation uses only three downstream tasks (small task set); potential domain/language coverage bias; not a saturated or widely standardized benchmark.
